sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Veenendaal charges for parking in a central zone A and keeps permit parking in the ring around it, zone B. The municipality's designation order, valid from 1 January 2024, regulates street parking from Monday to Saturday, 9:00 to 20:00, with Friday and other shopping evenings until 22:00 and Sundays free; the De Sterke Arm car park in zone B is paid as well as permit parking [0]. Three public garages, Arie van Hensbergen, Gemeentehuis and Tricotage, follow their own rules all day, and the order shows Sundays as free [1]. A permit decision of 2021 allows at most three resident permits per address, lets anyone request a garage permit and caps some addresses at zero street permits [10]. Policy documents point toward using existing parking better. The council adopted revised parking norms on 20 April 2023, allowing a mobility plan to cut the requirement of new developments by at most 25 percent [8]. The parking vision of 2013, now old, found no overall shortage in the centre and concluded that a park-and-ride would add no value [9][13].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The municipality is modernising its garages and charging. In July 2022 it awarded new parking equipment with licence-plate recognition for three garages to Taxameter Centrale for 912,301 euros excluding VAT, aimed at letting drivers pay afterwards without a barrier, with Tricotage last, planned for January 2023 [11]. Traffic decisions designate thirteen locations with two charging spaces each in December 2025, because of heavy use of existing posts [15], and nine more in April 2026, seven following requests from drivers without private parking, which take effect once the post and signs are in place [14]. The 2013 vision wanted a better route-information system and a parking app [12].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality owns and runs the on-street parking and some garages; a 2021 notice lists about 1,700 public spaces in the centre, about 4,800 regulated spaces in the ring, the Gemeentehuis garage (156 spaces) and the Arie van Hensbergen garage (704 spaces), with Tricotage (1,008) to follow [5]. A competition decision of 26 September 2017 records that Q-Park runs two garages in the centre, Passage and Corridor, with 780 paid spaces [6], and found that the municipality had not charged full costs in its own garages from 2014 to 2016 [7]. For 2026 the tariff is 2.94 euros an hour on the street and 2.50 euros in the garages, with a daily maximum of 8.00 euros and 9.50 euros on Saturdays [2][3]. A first resident permit costs 79.28 euros a year, and the fine is 82.00 euros [4]. The national register holds live feeds for Scheepjeshof, Duivenweide and Gemeentehuis, but the Gemeentehuis feed declares 9,999 spaces, which is not real [16].

Our data are mixed. The Scheepjeshof garage, with 61 days since 22 August 2026, is the one usable series; our records give it 470 spaces, but its free count never exceeded 395, the register's capacity, and on that basis occupancy averaged about 36% on weekdays and 44% at weekends. The Duivenweide feed shows only two different values in 45 days and stopped on 8 October, and the Gemeentehuis feed shows a constant zero free spaces for its three days, so we do not treat either as a measurement.
